lessons.title: Diagnostic
lessons.gap: What ___ you do for a living?
lessons.passage: Maya starts work at seven in a small factory. She is a software technician, but she also helps the maintenance team. Every morning, she checks the messages from the night shift. Today, a new colleague from Canada visits the factory. He wants to know how the testing station works. Maya feels nervous because she does not often speak English at work. Instead of translating every word, she asks short questions and listens carefully. Her colleague speaks slowly and shows her the equipment. At the end of the visit, Maya writes three useful expressions in her notebook. She decides to practice them again tomorrow.
lessons.question: What does Maya check?
lessons.prompt: Introduce yourself and explain why you need English.
lessons.explanation: Usa do con I/you/we/they y does con he/she/it. Después de does el verbo vuelve a su forma base. Con be no se usa do.
lessons.examples: Do you work here? / Does she test sensors? / Are you ready?

reading.question: Why does Maya feel nervous?
options: She rarely speaks English at work.
reading.evidence: She does not often speak English at work.

lessons.writing: Introduce yourself in 80 words. Explain your job, interests and reason for studying English.
lessons.listening: Do you work with machines? I work with software, but I also help the maintenance team. What about you?

lessons.title: Meet a colleague
lessons.gap: I ___ an engineer.
lessons.passage: Nina is a new engineer at a company that makes electrical equipment. Her first day is busy, but her colleagues are friendly. Her desk is next to a testing area. A colleague called Leo shows her the office and introduces her to the production supervisor. Their team is responsible for checking new products before they leave the factory. Nina has a small notebook with questions. She is interested in the software, but she is not familiar with the machines yet. At lunch, Leo asks about her interests. Nina explains that she enjoys building robots and learning about different cultures. They agree to have lunch together again.
lessons.question: Where is Alex's desk?
lessons.prompt: Introduce yourself to Alex and ask two questions.
lessons.explanation: Am, is y are describen identidad, estado y ubicación. My, your, his, her, our y their van antes del sustantivo.
lessons.examples: I am an engineer. / Her desk is near the door. / Their tools are new.

reading.question: Where is Nina’s desk?
reading.evidence: Her desk is next to a testing area.

lessons.writing: Write a friendly introduction to a new colleague. Use five possessives.
lessons.listening: Hi, I am Leo. This is our office. Your desk is near the testing area. Are you ready to meet the team?

lessons.title: Daily routine
lessons.gap: She ___ the equipment every morning.
lessons.passage: Daniel works in a small repair shop. He arrives at eight and opens his computer before he starts any repairs. His first task is to read the messages from customers. Some customers need new parts, while others need help with software. Daniel makes a list of the most urgent problems and shares it with his colleague. They usually take a short break at eleven. In the afternoon, Daniel tests the repaired equipment and writes a summary of his work. He does not leave until he checks the next day’s appointments. On Fridays, the team reviews its results and discusses ways to improve the service.
lessons.question: What does Laura write after lunch?
lessons.prompt: Describe your usual workday.
lessons.explanation: Present simple: rutinas y hechos. Agrega -s o -es a he/she/it. En negativas usa do not o does not + verbo base.
lessons.examples: I check reports. / She checks reports. / He does not check reports.

correction.bad: He check the machine every day.
correction.good: He checks the machine every day.

reading.question: What does Daniel write after testing the equipment?
reading.evidence: He tests the repaired equipment and writes a summary.

lessons.writing: Write 100 words about your daily routine and how it differs on weekends.
lessons.listening: I usually arrive at eight. My colleague starts at nine. We check messages before we repair any equipment.

lessons.title: Describe a place
lessons.gap: There ___ two robots in the room.
lessons.passage: A small workshop has two main areas. Near the entrance, there is a desk with a computer and a printer. On the left, there are three shelves with spare parts. A toolbox is under the workbench, and a set of cables is next to it. At the back of the room, there is a small test station. Visitors cannot enter that area without permission. The workshop manager wants to improve the layout because people sometimes have trouble finding tools. She asks the team to label the shelves and keep the walking area clear. At the end of the week, they will review the changes together.
lessons.question: Where is the toolbox?
lessons.prompt: Describe your room or workshop in six sentences.
lessons.explanation: There is presenta un objeto singular o incontable; there are presenta objetos plurales. Para preguntar invierte is/are y there.
lessons.examples: There is a toolbox. / There are three cables. / Is there a spare motor?

reading.question: Why does the manager want to change the layout?
options: Tools are sometimes difficult to find.
reading.evidence: People sometimes have trouble finding tools.

lessons.writing: Describe a workshop layout in 100 words and suggest two improvements.

lessons.title: New teammate
lessons.gap: We ___ testing a new sensor now.
lessons.passage: Today, the production team is preparing a new testing station. Sara is connecting a computer, and Tomas is reading the installation instructions. Their supervisor is talking to a supplier on the phone. Normally, the team tests old products in the morning, but today they are working on a new model. A technician is looking for a cable that is missing from the kit. Sara checks the parts list and finds a similar cable in a drawer. Before they connect it, the team confirms that it matches the required specifications. They are not rushing because a careful installation can prevent problems later in the project.

lessons.explanation: Present continuous: am/is/are + verbo-ing para acciones en progreso. Present simple para rutinas.

correction.good: We are testing a sensor now.

reading.question: What is Tomas doing?
reading.evidence: Tomas is reading the installation instructions.

lessons.title: Music and friendship
lessons.gap: I ___ help you tomorrow.
lessons.passage: Emma is worried about a presentation in English. She has practiced the introduction many times, but she still feels nervous when people ask unexpected questions. Her friend Oliver offers to help. He promises to listen to her presentation after work and ask three questions. Emma agrees to practice with him instead of memorizing every sentence. They make a simple plan: first, she will explain the project; then, Oliver will ask about its purpose and results. Finally, she will write down expressions that she wants to remember. Emma realizes that a good friend does not need to give perfect answers. Sometimes, listening patiently is enough to help someone improve.
lessons.question: How do the friends stay in touch?
lessons.prompt: Describe a promise you would make to a friend.
lessons.explanation: Will + verbo base expresa promesas, decisiones espontáneas y predicciones. La negación es will not o won’t.
lessons.examples: I will call you. / She won’t forget. / Will you help me?

reading.question: How will Oliver help Emma?
options: He will listen and ask questions.
reading.evidence: He promises to listen and ask three questions.

lessons.writing: Write a dialogue in which two friends make promises and offer support.

lessons.passage: A candidate asks about the team, training opportunities and expectations. These questions help her understand whether the position matches her goals.

lessons.title: Psychology reading
lessons.gap: ___ the task was difficult, participants persisted.
lessons.passage: People remember information better when they retrieve it rather than simply reread it. Retrieval requires effort, but that effort can strengthen memory. Researchers distinguish immediate performance from long-term learning.
lessons.question: What can strengthen memory?
lessons.prompt: Explain why practice can feel difficult yet be useful.
lessons.explanation: Práctica de Contrast. Completa la frase y compara con el modelo.

lessons.title: AI reading
lessons.gap: The data were incomplete; ___, the result was uncertain.
lessons.passage: An algorithm can detect patterns in examples, but biased data may lead to unreliable predictions. Engineers evaluate models on new data to estimate how well they generalize.

lessons.readingAnswer: to estimate how well they generalize

lessons.title: Evidence and opinion
lessons.gap: The proposal is useful; ___, it has limitations.
lessons.passage: A city considers replacing buses with electric vehicles. The proposal may reduce local pollution, but it requires charging infrastructure. Decision makers must compare benefits with costs and practical constraints.

lessons.title: Assessment B
lessons.gap: The project succeeded because the team ___ effectively.
lessons.passage: A research team tested a new device and found promising results. Although the prototype worked in controlled conditions, its performance in real environments remains uncertain. More evidence is required before deployment.
lessons.question: What remains uncertain?
lessons.prompt: Summarize evidence, limitations and next steps.

lessons.title: Past decisions
lessons.gap: If we had tested earlier, we would have ___ the fault.
lessons.passage: A product launch was delayed because a supplier missed a deadline. In retrospect, the team could have qualified a backup supplier earlier. The experience changed its procurement strategy.

lessons.title: Business crisis
lessons.gap: If we had planned better, we ___ be less stressed now.
lessons.passage: A company faces a shortage of components. Earlier purchasing decisions limited its options, and the current team must balance urgent demand against quality risks.

lessons.title: Reasoning checkpoint

lessons.passage: A device worked in the laboratory but failed after transport. The engineers suspect mechanical stress, though they have not ruled out a software issue. Further tests are needed.

lessons.title: Astronomy
lessons.gap: The observations ___ suggest the presence of ice.
lessons.passage: Some lunar regions remain in shadow for long periods. Remote measurements can suggest the presence of water ice, but interpreting these signals requires care. Surface conditions and instrument limitations influence the conclusions.

lessons.title: Scientific hypothesis
lessons.gap: The ___ of the system requires more testing.
lessons.passage: A hypothesis is a testable explanation, not merely a guess. Researchers specify expected observations and compare them with actual results. Unexpected findings may motivate a revised explanation.
lessons.question: What makes a hypothesis different from a guess?
lessons.prompt: Propose a testable hypothesis.
lessons.explanation: Práctica de Nominalisation. Completa la frase y compara con el modelo.

lessons.title: Research results
lessons.gap: ___ the results, the researchers revised their hypothesis.
lessons.passage: The experiment compared two cooling methods. One reduced temperature faster but consumed more energy. The researchers noted that the best method depends on the operating requirements.

lessons.title: Lecture summary
lessons.gap: The findings are believed ___ support the theory.
lessons.passage: A lecture explains how cities form heat islands. Dark surfaces absorb sunlight, while vegetation provides shade and evaporative cooling. Urban design can influence local temperatures, although climate and geography also matter.

lessons.title: Abstract writing

lessons.passage: A study compares two sensor calibration methods under controlled conditions. The authors report improved repeatability with one method, but caution that further validation is necessary in industrial settings.

lessons.explanation: Práctica de Concise academic style. Completa la frase y compara con el modelo.

lessons.title: Innovation pitch

lessons.passage: A team proposes a low-cost assistive device. Its value depends not only on the initial price but also on reliability, maintenance and usability. User feedback guides the design process.

lessons.title: Academic checkpoint
lessons.gap: The results are promising, ___ preliminary.
lessons.passage: A pilot study reports a possible benefit, but its participants were few and the observation period was short. The authors recommend a larger study before making broad claims.

lessons.title: AI debate
lessons.gap: Not only ___ the tool save time, but it also introduced errors.
lessons.passage: AI can accelerate routine tasks, yet efficiency is not equivalent to reliability. In high-stakes settings, human review remains important because plausible outputs may conceal mistakes.
lessons.question: Why is human review important?
lessons.prompt: Debate the role of AI in engineering.

lessons.title: Counterargument

lessons.passage: A policy proposal appears attractive at first, but its effects vary across communities. Supporters emphasize efficiency, whereas critics point to unequal access. A fair evaluation considers both perspectives.

lessons.title: Weak evidence
lessons.gap: The evidence is insufficient to ___ a causal link.
lessons.passage: Two variables changed at the same time, but that does not establish that one caused the other. A third factor may explain both observations. Controlled comparisons can help distinguish these possibilities.

lessons.title: Figurative language

lessons.title: Cumulative 5

lessons.title: Music metaphors
